title: Compute adiabatic occupation and tunneling rate
action: Compute the solvent-coordinate-dependent adsorbate occupation ⟨n_a(q)⟩ and the tunneling rate k(q) for a representative parameter set (broadenings Δ1=Δ2=0.01 eV, reorganization energy λ=0.6 eV, bias V_b=0.2 V, overpotential η=0) using the adiabatic resonant tunneling formulas. Evaluate at q from 0 to 1 in steps of 0.01 and save the results to adiabatic_quantities.csv.
description: Adiabatic occupation and tunneling rate as functions of the solvent coordinate for a representative parameter set.
output_schema: Columns: q (float, dimensionless solvent coordinate from 0 to 1), occupation (float, dimensionless), rate (float, arbitrary units as defined in the paper).

title: Run stochastic molecular dynamics and compute average current
action: Implement the collision-model stochastic molecular dynamics algorithm described in the paper to propagate the solvent coordinate on the adiabatic potential-energy surface E(q) (derived from the occupation) while evaluating the instantaneous rate k(q). Run simulations for the configurations presented in the paper: (1) current vs bias for λ = 0.2, 0.4, 0.6 eV, Δ1=Δ2=0.01 eV, η ≈ 0, sweeping bias; (2) current vs overpotential for λ = 0.2, 0.4, 0.6 eV, Δ1=Δ2=0.01 eV, V_b=0.1 V; (3) current vs overpotential for Δ1=0.01 V, Δ2=0.001 V, V_b=0.05 V, and λ = 0.2, 0.4, 0.6 eV (matching the experimental conditions discussed in the paper). For each run, simulate long enough to achieve several thousand barrier crossings and compute the time-averaged electron current. Save all results to current_results.csv.
description: Average electron tunneling current for all required parameter sets (current vs. bias and current vs. overpotential curves).
output_schema: Columns: scenario (string, e.g. 'fig4_lambda_0.2', 'fig6_lambda_0.4', 'fig7_lambda_0.6'), independent_variable (string, e.g. 'V_b=0.05' or 'eta=-0.3'), independent_value (float, V), current (float, normalized to arbitrary units as in the paper).
